item.title: Tai Po fire: Taxes, utility bills, hospital fees waived for owners, residents affected by blaze
item.description: The Hong Kong government has waived taxes and utility fees for property owners and residents affected by the fatal Wang Fuk Court fire which claimed the lives of 159 people. item.title: Hong Kong gov’t hits out at news agency AFP, says media mogul Jimmy Lai being cared for in prison
item.description: Hong Kong authorities have hit out at news agency Agence France-Presse (AFP) over an article about pro-democracy media mogul Jimmy Lai, currently detained as he awaits the verdict of his national security trial. item.title: Tai Po fire: Living subsidy for affected residents doubled to HK$100,000
item.description: The living subsidy for residents affected by the deadly Tai Po blaze will be doubled from HK$50,000 to HK$100,000, the Hong Kong government has announced. item.title: Displaced residents wish to return to Wang Fuk Court after fatal fire but face uncertain future
item.description: Residents of the only block that escaped the deadly blaze at Tai Po’s Wang Fuk Court have said they would like to return to their homes in the future, but the prospect is clouded by uncertainty. item.title: Taiwan to suspend access to Chinese app Xiaohongshu over online fraud
item.description: Taiwan will temporarily block access to the popular Chinese social media app Xiaohongshu after detecting hundreds of online shopping fraud cases, the democratic island’s Criminal Investigation Bureau said on Thursday. item.description: Hong Kong’s anti-graft watchdog has arrested four men for allegedly making online posts or comments to incite others to boycott or cast invalid ballots in the “patriots only” Legislative Council (LegCo) elections on Sunday. item.title: Tai Po fire: Almost 400 pets rescued from Wang Fuk Court
item.description: More pets have been rescued from the Wang Fuk Court housing complex, nine days on from last Wednesday’s deadly blaze.
